hook: Marc Benioff founded Salesforce in March 1999 and has been its Chair and CEO ever since, twenty-seven years in the same seat. He spent the thirteen years before that at Oracle, rising to Senior Vice President, and interned at Apple in 1984 writing example assembly programs for the Macintosh 68000 Development System. Salesforce made subscription cloud delivery the normal way enterprises buy software, and it now matters to AI for a structural reason rather than a model one: the company holds the customer data and permission model that an enterprise agent needs before it can take an action anyone would trust.

standing.watch: The records leave much unresolved. The only news story is dated 2026-10-10 and concerns Trump's AI rebrand catching on with Elon Musk and Marc Benioff, but it gives no further detail about what that means for Salesforce or for him. No pending case, planned listing or dispute appears in the records supplied. What is coming next, according to these records, is simply the continued influence of Salesforce's data and permission model in enterprise AI, and whatever the named story develops into.
standing.record: The records describe a long career before and after Salesforce: thirteen years at Oracle, rising to Senior Vice President, and an internship at Apple in 1984 writing example assembly programs for the Macintosh 68000 Development System. Salesforce made subscription cloud delivery the normal way enterprises buy software, and the site frames its AI relevance as structural rather than model-based. His philanthropy, the 1-1-1 model created on day one, has been adopted by more than 20,000 companies. He holds a BS in Business Administration from the University of Southern California and sits on its Board of Trustees, was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 2019, and received the Yale Legend in Leadership Award and the Colin Powell Distinguished Leadership Award in 2024. The single news story ties him to a political rebranding of AI alongside Elon Musk.
standing.standing: Marc Benioff stands as the founder, Chair and CEO of Salesforce, a company he started in March 1999 and has led for twenty-seven years. His influence in artificial intelligence comes through Salesforce's position in enterprise software, where the company holds customer data and the permission model that an enterprise agent needs before it can act. He also owns and co-chairs TIME, sits on the World Economic Forum Board of Trustees, and was the inaugural Chair of its Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution in San Francisco. The site's records show one news story naming him, about Trump's AI rebrand catching on with Elon Musk and Marc Benioff.

quick_facts: Founded Salesforce in March 1999 and serves as Chair and CEO, twenty-seven years in post
Senior Vice President at Oracle from 1986 to 1999, thirteen years before founding Salesforce
Interned at Apple in 1984, writing example assembly programs for the Macintosh 68000 Development System
BS in Business Administration from the University of Southern California, where he sits on the Board of Trustees
Created the 1-1-1 philanthropy model on day one, committing one percent of equity, product and employee time; more than 20,000 companies have since adopted it
Elected a member of the National Academy of Engineering in 2019
Named a Chevalier de la Legion d'honneur; received the Yale Legend in Leadership Award and the Colin Powell Distinguished Leadership Award in 2024

achievements.title: Salesforce
achievements.impact: Founded in 1999 and built into the largest enterprise applications company in the world and the leading provider of CRM software, with more than 70,000 employees.

achievements.title: The software-as-a-service model
achievements.impact: Pioneered subscription cloud delivery for enterprise applications, replacing licensed on-premise installation as the industry default.

achievements.title: The 1-1-1 model and Pledge 1%
achievements.impact: Committed one percent of Salesforce equity, product and employee time to the community from the company's first day, and co-founded the Pledge 1% movement that carried the model to more than 20,000 companies.

achievements.title: Agentforce
achievements.impact: Salesforce's agent platform, positioned around grounding AI action in a company's own data, permissions and governance rather than model capability alone.

achievements.title: National Academy of Engineering
achievements.impact: Elected a member in 2019, a recognition more often given to researchers than to company founders.
